question: Which Gupta ruler was also known as 'Vikramaditya'?
options: Chandragupta II (reigned c. 375–415 CE) assumed the title Vikramaditya ('Sun of Valour').
explanation: Chandragupta II (reigned c. 375–415 CE) assumed the title Vikramaditya ('Sun of Valour').

question: 'Periods of peace support the development of sociocultural life, literature, and science.' Examine this statement regarding the Gupta Empire.
options: Gupta political stability and economic wealth allowed kings to patronize scholars, scientists, and artists. Without war
explanation: Gupta political stability and economic wealth allowed kings to patronize scholars, scientists, and artists. Without war disruption, Aryabhata made mathematical discoveries, Kalidasa authored poetry, universities like Nalanda flourished, and artists carved Sarnath sculptures and Ajanta murals.

question: Elaborate on the scientific and technological achievements during the Gupta period.
options: 1. Astronomy: Aryabhata established that Earth rotates on its axis and causes day/night, providing true shadow causes fo
explanation: 1. Astronomy: Aryabhata established that Earth rotates on its axis and causes day/night, providing true shadow causes for eclipses. 2. Mathematics: Formulated pi estimates, square/cube roots, and place-value system rules. 3. Metallurgy: Cast large bronze Buddhas and the Mehrauli Iron Pillar which remains rust-free after 1600 years. 4. Medicine & Surgery: Compilations of Ayurvedic texts and surgical procedures. 5. Higher Education: Flourishing of residential universities like Nalanda.
